item.title: Carrick roundabout nearly fully repaired after crash damage
item.description: Major damage to a roundabout in Carrick-on-Shannon, after a late-night crash, is almost entirely fixed. A car failed to stop for the gardai at around 2.30 on Sunday morning, and then collided with the Shannon roundabout. The driver, a man in his 30s, was arrested and is due before the courts soon. Advertisement Carrick Tidy Towns chairman, John Gaffey, says the roundabout was badly damaged: He says only a small bit of more work is needed on the roundabout: Advertisement

item.title: Refugees spend an average of a year in Ballagh Eroc
item.description: Refugees spend an average of 12 months in Ballaghaderreen's Eroc Centre. The Department of Justice says 175 people live in the Abbeyfield Hotel Emergency Reception and Orientation Centre. 167 are from Syria, and eight are from Afghanistan. item.title: Only three local gardai appointed to Roads Policing Unit last year
item.description: Just three gardaí were appointed to the Roads Policing Unit locally in 2025. An Garda Síochána missed its staff commitments for roads policing for the second year in a row. The former Garda Commissioner, Drew Harris, promised 150 new traffic officers over the last two years - but only delivered 79. item.title: Only 19 small roads addressed under LIS in Leitrim last year
item.description: Only 19 roads in Co Leitrim were addressed under the Local Improvement Scheme in 2025. The scheme involves the state and homeowners jointly paying for the upgrade of small roads and laneways. The Department of Rural Development have allocated over €900,000 to the county under the scheme, while there are 120 roads are yet to be completed in the county. item.title: 58 admitted patients stranded on trolleys in Sligo hospital
item.description: There were almost 70 admitted patients waiting for a bed at local hospitals this morning. That's according to the INMO's latest trolley watch report. Wednesday's figures show there were 58 patients waiting in Sligo University Hospital. Advertisement This included 40 in the emergency department and 18 on wards elsewhere. While there were 8 patients waiting in the Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar.

item.title: Pat Forde elected as chair of Leitrim Local Community Safety Partnership
item.description: Pat Forde has been elected as the chairperson of Leitrim Local Community Safety Partnership. He was chosen at their first meeting in the Landmark Hotel in Carrick-on-Shannon in recent days. The Community Safety Partnerships are set up with the aim to combat anti-social behaviour and criminality by creating a tailored local community safety plan with input from the local community and public services. South Leitrim councillor Maeve Reynolds was elected as vice-chairperson. Advertisement

item.title: More clinics needed in Roscommon & east Galway for children with mental illnesses - Daly
item.description: A Fianna Fáil TD says more clinics are needed in Roscommon and east Galway for children with mental illnesses. The Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service in Roscommon town serves all of Co Roscommon and east Galway. It's almost at full capacity. Local CAMHS management want to buy a new building in Roscommon town to cater for more people - but the HSE has rejected it. Deputy Martin Daly says more accommodation is needed: Advertisement

item.title: Standing orders suspended briefly at today's Longford County Council meeting
item.description: Standing orders were suspended for 15 minutes at this afternoons meeting of Longford County Council. The move was made in solidarity with Gardaí and emergency services following Monday nights double stabbing in the county town. Two men suffered serious injuries and were hospitalised following the incident. Fine Gael Cllr Niall Gannon says the town and wider county is feeling the effects: Advertisement

item.title: Man charged with causing damage to Athlone Garda Station expected to bring a full bail application before the court
item.description: A man charged with causing significant damage to Athlone Garda Station and a number of Garda vehicles using a beer keg is expected to bring a full bail application before the court after his former partner offered up her home in Ballinasloe as an address at which he can reside. item.title: Councillor criticises decision to exclude Longford town from new short-term-let laws
item.description: A Fianna Fáil councillor is criticising the decision to exclude Longford town from new short-term-let laws. The clampdown on Airbnbs and similar properties was going to apply to towns with over 20,000 people - but that's now down to 10,000. This means Longford town will be excluded. The new rules are aimed at freeing up more rental accommodation. Longford councillor Uruemu Adejinmi says the government is wrong to water them down: Advertisement
